sentences.text:
2. By the impugned Judgment and Decree, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,19,000/-
together with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of deposit, to the appellant/claimant.
Aggrieved by the same, the present Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellant/claimant for enhancement of compensation.

J.Nagapushpam vs U.Syed Mohideen on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43717015/
1 3.

The accident is said to have been taken place on 11.11.2016 at about 11.30 a.m., when the appellant was walking from south to north direction in Rajaji Salai near Clive Battery Company, at that time,
the 1st respondent's motorcycle bearing Registration No.TN.11-D-4963 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the appellant, due to which, the appellant had sustained grievous injuries and was admitted in the hospital.
At the time of accident, the appellant was aged about 54 years and was selling clothes and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

Due to the injuries https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3/9 C.M.A.No.4186 of sustained by the appellant in the accident,
she could not able to continue her business and therefore, claimed a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- as compensation.

4. The Tribunal after considering the pleadings, oral and documentary evidence, held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent.

At the same time, the Tribunal has fixed 10% negligence on the part of the appellant on the ground that the appellant/claimant tried to cross the road in a non- pedestrian crossing at the time of accident was well supported by the First Information Report as well as the rough sketch.
Therefore, the Tribunal directed the second respondent-Insurance Company, to pay a sum of Rs.5,19,000/- towards 90% of the award amount as compensation to the appellant.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal erred in fixing 10%
contributory negligence on the part of the appellant and therefore deducted 10% of compensation.

The appellant sustained injuries with left leg tibia and fracture of right leg and ankle and after surgery of ankle and tibia bone fracture and the Tribunal ought to have adopted multiplier for awarding compensation.

The amounts awarded by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4/9 C.M.A.No.4186 of Tribunal under different heads are meagre and prayed for setting aside the portion of the award fixing 10% contributory negligence on the part of the appellant as well as for enhancement of compensation.
6. The learned counsel for the respondent submits that the Tribunal has rightly fixed 10% negligence on the part of the appellant.
The amounts awarded by the Tribunal under different heads are not meagre and the appellant has not made out any case for enhancement of compensation and is therefore liable to be dismissed.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the second respondent and also perused the material evidence on record.
8.
From the materials available on record, it is seen that the Tribunal has held that the accident has occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the rider /first respondent.
The appellant had sustained fracture of ankle and tibia bone fracture.

She has taken treatment as in patient at Chennai,
National Hospital from 11.11.2016 to 12.11.2016 and thereafter she underwent s surgery  ankle spanning external ring fixtor application on the left leg on 14.11.2016 and she was discharged on 28.11.2016.

Further, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5/9 C.M.A.No.4186 of again she was admitted for treatment at Sri Hospital on 25.01.2017 to 28.01.017 , she underwent a surgery on 26.01.2017, with the procedure done, states s  External fixator removal left tibia and  Pin tract debridement left leg.........

Again on 16.02.2017, she was admitted in Sri Hospitals, she underwent J.Nagapushpam vs U.Syed Mohideen on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43717015/
2 surgery on 18.02.2017, with the procedure stated as  ORIF with 7 holed didstal tibia LCP for lft tibia with iliac crest bone grafting and  ORIF with 7 hole/1/3rd tubular plate for left fibula
and she was discharged on 27.02.2017.

Ex.C.1 is the disability certificate issued by the Regional Medical Board,
Kilpauk Medical College Hospital, Chennai, in which it is stated that the disability of the petitioner is post traumatic sequale of left leg due to the injury on the left ankle-comminuted pilon and lateral mallcoli and the Medical Board has determined the disability as 35%.
9.

entities.text:
Regional Medical Board,
Kilpauk Medical College Hospital, Chennai
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the appellant/claimant had sustained fracture of right leg and ankle and considering the fact that the age of the appellant/claimant was about 54 years at the time of accident, as she could not able to continue her business.
Therefore, Rs.5,000/- per percentage of disability is granted and hereby, a sum of Rs.1,75,000/- is awarded towards permanent disability.

Since there is a contributory negligence as 10% on the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6/9 C.M.A.No.4186 of part of the appellant and 90% contributory negligence on the part of the second respondent- Insurance Company, is not disturbed.
At the same time, the compensation awarded towards under the other heads require interference as the Tribunal has awarded the lesser amount.

10. Consequently, I am inclined to modify the compensation awarded under the various heads as follows:

 Pain and sufferings 50,000 75,000 Enhan  loss of amenities 30,000 30,000 Confi  Medical Expenses 3,01,405 3,01,405 Confir  Loss of Income 36,000 36,000 Confi  Transport expenses 10,000 15,000 Enhan  Extra nourishment 25,000 25,000 Confir  Attendant charges 17,200 21,500 Enhan  Damage to clothes 2,000 2,000 Confir  5,76,605 6,80,905  * Total award amount : Rs. 6,80,905.00 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  7/9 C.
 Less 10% negligence on the  part of the appellant : Rs. 68,090.50  -------------
 Net Amount : Rs. 6,12,814.
 --------------
J.Nagapushpam vs U.Syed Mohideen on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43717015/
3  Rounded off to Rs.6,10,
11.

Accordingly, this civil miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and 90% liability is fixed on the second respondent/ Insurance Company and the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.5,19,000/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.6,10,000/- together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of such deposit.
The appellant is directed to pay necessary Court fee, if any, on the enhanced compensation.

Therefore, the second respondent- Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced award amount now determined by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the same with proportionate interest and costs, less the amount if any,
already withdrawn, by filing suitable application before the Tribunal.
No costs.
